plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: Clouds of blush-white blossoms cover bare branches before the leaves appear. Petals drift down like confetti in spring breezes and carpet paths and parks in soft pink.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in the Washington, D.C. area. Peak bloom usually falls in late March or early April, and some blossoms linger into mid-April.
plants.location: Tidal Basin, Washington, D.C., USA, and temperate parks across the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: The famous trees around Washington's Tidal Basin were a gift from Tokyo in 1912. Each tree's flowering window is short, often only a week or so, which is part of why people treasure it.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Cup-shaped blooms in bold, saturated colors stand upright on smooth stems above blue-green leaves. Whole fields turn into bands of crimson, gold and magenta.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-April is typically the heart of the season in the Netherlands, with fields in full color from early to late April.
plants.location: Bulb fields of the Netherlands, such as those near Lisse, and gardens across northern Europe
plants.funFact: In the 1630s, tulip bulbs fetched such high prices in the Dutch Republic that the episode became known as 'tulip mania'. It is often cited as one of the first speculative bubbles.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: Slender stems carry clusters of wavy, spidery pink petals that shimmer as if dusted with glitter. They bloom while the foliage is mostly absent, which gives them a dramatic, almost theatrical look.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering from roughly March to May. April 12 falls within that period.
plants.location: Southern Africa's eastern highlands, including the Drakensberg region of South Africa, where it is native
plants.funFact: The sparkle on the petals comes from tiny cells in the petal surface that reflect light. The plant is a bulb that is native to rocky mountain slopes.
